page.layout: One printed page (p. 295), running text in one column. Running head across the top. Two marginal notes in the right margin, beside the paragraphs at "patribus" and "sacrificia". Page number at top right. Signature mark at foot. The left edge of the scan shows part of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: sia, & Dei populo, de quibus 1. Sam.28.verf.8. 2.Reg.i.v.2. 2.Reg.21.Esa.8.v.19. Act.16.v.18.legimus, quibus idololatrici cultus, pluralitas deorum,injustæ cædes, rapinæ, fœdæ libidines, mactationes hominum, aliaque turpissima flagitia mandata & stabilita fuerunt. Pleraq; tamen oracula amphiboliis & ænigmatibus sunt involuta, vel quia de eventibus dubitârunt dæmones; vel ut odio generis humani, & nocendi studio tegant atque occultét veritatem. Delectatur enim Diabolus mendaciis & pernicie nostrâ, lætaturq; calamitatibus nostris. Ideo talibus ludit ænigmatibus.

Quartò, quemadmodum Deus patribus, pa4. Appari-tiones visi-biles Dia-boli.-triarchis & prophetis sæpe apparuit, cumq; ipsis locutus est, assumptâ visibili specie, & formis, quæ rebus illis, quas cum ipsis agere constituerat, attemperatæ erant; ita Diabolus quoque veneficis vel maleficis certâ quadam, & tetrâ atque deformi figurâ, vel atri hominis, vel hirci, vel equi, & sic deinceps apparet, cumq; illis sermones & colloquia miscet, quas formas & corpora ex aëre condensato & rarefacto assumit, quemadmodum per aërem sermones etiam suos effor-mat.

Quintò, quemadmodum Deus in ecclesia sa-5. Sacrificia fagarū dia-bolica.crificia instituit, in quibus, præscripto ab ipso modo, pecudes mactatæ, in certas partes divisæ, & igne cælesti consumptæ fuerunt, ad præfigurandum Christi cruentum sacrificium: ita varia quoque inter ethnicos sacrificiorum genera monstravit Diabolus, quibus ipsum coluerunt, ut

page.notes: The page is a clean print. The marginal notes are printed in small type and are transcribed in place. The left edge shows the neighbouring page's text and was left out. The word at the end of the last line is "ut", with a slight mark on the t that could be a ţ ligature; it is read as "ut". The fragment "sia," at the start is the end of a word continued from the previous page; it stays as printed. The cited verses (1. Sam.28.verf.8, 2.Reg.i.v.2, 2.Reg.21.Esa.8.v.19, Act.16.v.18) are copied as printed.
